summary: My Profile: overview, organization chart and account settings
description: A My Profile page for every signed-in person (route /profile, reached from a Profile link in the account menu): Overview (name, role, email, manager), Organization (a live reporting chart built from the real users.manager_id relationships: an employee sees their manager above, themselves highlighted and any direct reports below; a manager sees their own manager and everyone under them with collapsible levels; an HR Admin browses the whole company, loading level by level) and Account settings (a secure Change password form). Additive: no role changes and no existing page changes beyond the Profile link. DECIDED with the user on 2026-10-19: NO department or job title (the users table has neither and only managers and employees exist), NO dark mode and no Appearance card (AGENTS.md keeps the UI light-only), NO profile pages for other people (the manager card is plain text and chart boxes are not links). TASK-026 (change password, EPIC-2) is superseded by TASK-065. The chart reads live with no cache, so it follows a manager change on the next load; until EPIC-8 lets HR change reporting lines only SQL changes them. Reference: the user's ChatGPT mockup (profile, organization, account settings), restyled with the app's tokens and the role-based navigation (the mockup's sidebar items are not ours). Priority: after EPIC-7, before EPIC-8.

summary: Profile page shell, tabs and Overview
description: Route /profile under (app) (requireSession, every role) with the page header 'My Profile' and three route-based tabs, like the Team Approvals tabs (a <nav> with aria-current): Overview /profile, Organization /profile/organization, Account settings /profile/settings. Each tab is its own page, so each stays inside the page query budget (POOL_MAX - 1). A 'Profile' link in the account menu (a client component) is the entry point, and the top bar title reads 'My Profile' on these pages (currentNavItem only knows nav items, so it needs a small case). Overview: an initials avatar, the name, a role label in text (Employee, Manager, HR Admin), the email and the manager's name ('No manager' for the top of the chart), read in ONE statement (getProfile) scoped to the session user's id in the SQL, in a streamed section with its own failure note. No department, job title, photo or link to anyone else's profile. Mobile first: no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px, a long unbroken name wraps.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: every role sees their own name, role, email and their manager's name;AC2: a person with no manager reads 'No manager';AC3: the read is one statement, the page stays within the query budget and a failed read says so without breaking the page;AC4: a visitor without a session goes to /login, and there is no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px with a long unbroken name;AC5: the account menu has a Profile link and the tabs are keyboard usable with aria-current

summary: Organization chart reads, scoped by role in SQL
description: src/lib/leave/org.ts with reads scoped by the SESSION role and id in the SQL, never by a client id. Employee: their manager (one row), themselves and their direct reports. Manager: their own manager above, themselves, and everyone under them to a depth cap of 6 (a recursive CTE over users.manager_id; a path array stops a cycle, because the schema only blocks a person managing themselves), capped at 200 people with the true total. HR Admin: the top of the company (users with no manager) and, for any person, one page of direct reports with a count of each one's own reports (getOrgChildren, 50 per page). Each node is id, name, role and the number of direct reports, and nothing else: no email, no leave data. GET /api/org/children?parent=&page= for the HR expansion (withErrorHandling, zod, hr_admin only, 403 in the envelope for anyone else): a documented exception to AGENTS.md rule 3, like the override route, because HR's scope is the whole company; the parent id from the client is only a lookup key and the role gate is the authorization. Each read is ONE statement and read live with no cache, so a changed manager_id shows on the next load. Real-database tests with mutations, including a user from another team (Leo) and a cycle.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an employee gets exactly their manager, themselves and their direct reports, and a peer or another team's person never appears;AC2: a manager gets their whole subtree to the cap and never a person outside it, with the true total when capped;AC3: HR gets the roots and any person's children, 50 per page with counts, and a manager or employee calling the HR route gets 403 in the standard envelope;AC4: a cycle in the data ends at the cycle guard instead of looping, and moving a person to another manager changes the next read;AC5: each read is one statement, and with 800 users the HR reads and a manager subtree finish well inside the query deadline (figures in the retro)

description: The Organization tab as in the reference, restyled with the app's tokens. 'Your place in the organization': the manager card above, you highlighted (aria-current and a 'You' badge in text), a connector line, then 'Direct reports' with the empty state 'No direct reports' and a small 'Reporting line' legend; a side card 'Your manager' with name and role as plain text (no link). A manager sees their own manager above themselves and a collapsible tree below (native details/summary or a button with aria-expanded: levels beyond the first start collapsed and each node says how many people report to it). An HR Admin sees the company roots and expands a node to load its children from the HR route (a small client component, 'Show more' per 50, a busy and an error state per node, focus kept on the control). Server component by default, client only for the HR expansion. Indentation is capped so a deep tree cannot widen the page; names wrap; role is shown as text. The page stays within the query budget and a failed read says so without breaking the tab.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an employee sees their manager above, themselves highlighted and their direct reports below, or 'No direct reports';AC2: a manager sees their manager and a collapsible tree of everyone under them, keyboard usable with aria-expanded, and an HR Admin can expand any node and page through its reports;AC3: nothing in the chart links to another person's profile and no email or leave data is shown;AC4: no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px with a deep tree and a long unbroken name;AC5: a failed read or a failed expansion shows a message and leaves the rest of the page working

description: Account settings tab, 'Security' card with a Change password form: current password, new password, confirmation, labelled fields with show/hide, role=alert errors, a role=status success message, keyboard usable, 44px targets, no horizontal scroll. Done through our server because the CSP allows connect-src 'self' only: POST /api/account/password (withErrorHandling, zod body, a route handler per AGENTS.md rule 11, session user only): it checks the current password by signing the session's own email in again (Supabase signInWithPassword), then calls auth.updateUser with the new one and signs out the person's OTHER sessions. A wrong current password gives one generic error. The new password must match its confirmation, differ from the current one and meet the minimum (at least 8 characters and at most 72, and never below the Supabase project's own minimum, which the user must check). A mock-login session has no Supabase account: the tab shows 'Password change is not available with the demo login' and the route refuses it; how a mock session is told apart without changing the getSession() contract is decided in the plan. Add current_password and new_password to the logger's redaction list, and never log, return or store a password. Supabase rate-limits sign-in; whether to add an app-side limit is decided in the plan. Voluntary: nothing forces a change and nothing is emailed (forced change belongs to EPIC-8). Reuse one password form component so EPIC-8's /set-password page can use it.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a signed-in person with the right current password can set a new one and sign in with it afterwards;AC2: a wrong current password, a mismatched or too-short new password, or one equal to the current one is rejected with an inline error and nothing changes;AC3: a mock-login session sees the explanation and the route refuses it in the standard envelope;AC4: a visitor without a session gets 401, and no password appears in a response, a log line or a stored value (tested with the logger and the redaction list);AC5: the form is keyboard and screen-reader usable with no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px

description: End to end against a real Postgres (and a fake Auth server for the password route, the approach EPIC-8's validation also uses): the chart for each role from a seeded organization, a user from another team never appearing, a person moved to another manager changing the next read, a cycle ending safely; the query budget for the three profile pages (the layout adds none: the bell reads in the browser); a browser check as employee, manager and HR at 1440, 375 and 320 px (tabs, the three charts including a deep tree and a long unbroken name, change password success and failure, a mock session, keyboard only, no console or CSP error); an 800-user load check of the HR reads with timings and EXPLAIN plans in the retro (scratchpad database only, never staging); full quality gate; a retro; mark TASK-026 superseded in the retro too.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: each role's chart contains exactly the people it should on a real engine, and a user from another team never appears;AC2: the quality gate passes and the query budget stays green for every profile page;AC3: the browser check passes at 1440, 375 and 320 px for all roles;AC4: the HR reads with 800 users finish well inside the query deadline and the figures are recorded
